summary.text: Steve Scalise represents Louisiana's 1st Congressional District, which runs from the Northshore of Lake Pontchartrain to the New Orleans suburbs. A former software engineer and technology-company marketing executive, he served in the Louisiana Legislature before his 2008 election to Congress. He has been in House Republican leadership since 2014 and has been House Majority Leader since January 2023.

paragraphs.text: Scalise was born in 1965 in New Orleans, and his official biography describes him as a native of Jefferson Parish.
He graduated from Archbishop Rummel High School and from Louisiana State University, where he earned a degree in computer science with a minor in political science.
Before entering politics he worked as a software engineer and as a technology company marketing executive.

Scalise served in the Louisiana State Legislature from 1996 to 2008, according to his official biography; Ballotpedia lists service in both the Louisiana House of Representatives and the State Senate. He was elected to the U.S. House in 2008, succeeding Bobby Jindal in the 1st District.
In the House he served as Majority Whip from 2014 to 2018 and Minority Whip from 2019 to 2022, and he was elected House Majority Leader for the 118th and 119th Congresses.

His official biography says he led the effort to pass the RESTORE Act, signed into law in 2012, which dedicated most Clean Water Act fines from the Deepwater Horizon oil spill to Gulf Coast restoration.
Scalise was critically wounded at a congressional baseball practice shooting on June 14, 2017, and returned to Congress after his recovery.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Jennifer, have two children.
